title: Video style is decided by the first image: two reference images, 4 videos, style never drifts
summary: Feed an AI-generated image in as the video's first frame and the finished style follows the image completely. A realistic-looking image gives a realistic-looking video, an anime image gives an anime video, and the prompt cannot override it. Changing resolution only changes background detail and wait time; the character stays solid at both tiers

items.label: Z-Image ref → 0.4MP 544×736 · 70.4s —— The live-action cosplay look comes from the reference image. Watch the face and the twin tails: they never change
Z-Image ref → 0.6MP 672×896 · 125.7s —— Compare the background with the 0.4MP version: truss, light spots, and the lace hem come out sharper
Flux2 ref → 0.4MP 544×736 · 70.4s —— The cel-shaded anime style comes from the reference image. Check whether the sailor uniform colors drift
Flux2 ref → 0.6MP 672×896 · 125.6s —— The character stays solid at both tiers; the gains only show in background detail

stats: Took the two best-tier AI images at 0.6 MP (one live-action look, one anime look) and used each as the opening first frame of H3 image-to-video (fl2va). Same prompt, same seed (91720260). Output: 124 frames, 5.17s @24fps videos with native audio. Two resolution tiers × two styles = 4 videos
Decided only by the video resolution tier, not by which reference image was used: 0.4MP 70.4s ▮▮▮▮▮ vs 0.6MP 125.6s ▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮ (bar length is proportional to time)

Video style follows the first-frame reference image completely; the prompt cannot change it: the Z-Image live-action image yields a live-action cosplay video, the Flux2 anime image yields a cel-shaded anime video
Twin tails, sailor uniform, and colors stay stable through all 5.17 seconds, with no face swap and no costume change
What the two tiers differ on

The higher tier's gains sit mostly in the background: stage truss, audience light spots, and lace hem texture come out clearly sharper; the character itself stays solid at both 0.4MP and 0.6MP, with no visible difference
findings: Video style is decided by the first frame; the prompt cannot change the style assignment. This cross-checks the conclusion of the upstream text-to-image resolution sweep

Under the same seed (91720260), camera moves and the dance starting point correlate strongly with how the first frame is composed. Whatever is in the first frame and where it sits is where the video starts moving
Recommended flow: 0.1MP to test composition fast → 0.6MP for the best reference image → 0.6MP for the final video (about 126s)
